column1: # Every environment variable that a SHIPPED binary reads and that can weaken,
# fake or bypass a check must have a row here. `scripts/release_identity_gate.sh`
# scans the production sources for hatch-shaped names and fails when it finds
# one that is not registered. The registry is therefore not documentation: it is
# the thing that makes adding a silent hatch a build failure rather than a
# The reason this needs a list at all: the danger is not any one override, it is
# that nobody can answer "what can an environment variable do to an installed
# client?" without reading the whole tree. That question has to be answerable in
# one file, or the answer drifts.
#   4 LOCATION      file:line of the read (or of the constant that names it)
#   5 NOTE          what it does and why the enforcement is what it is
# ENFORCEMENT meanings, and what the gate does with each:
#   compiled-out  a release build cannot honour it at all. The strongest answer.
#                 The gate requires a test that asserts this in BOTH profiles.
#   loud          honoured, but prints an unmissable line first. Acceptable for
#                 hatches whose effect the operator has to see anyway.
#   silent        honoured with no trace. NOT acceptable for anything that
#                 changes a security or hardware verdict; each row here is an
#                 open defect with a named owner, not a decision.
#   config        ordinary configuration that happens to match the name shape;
#                 it cannot weaken a check. Registered so the scan stays quiet
# ⚠ `frozen` rows are the ds4/ds4x code that is blocked from every build
# (CLAUDE.md hard constraint 1). They are registered so the scanner has a
# truthful answer for them, not because they can be reached.

Makes the NVML probe report no driver. On Windows it prints an explicit "*** TEST OVERRIDE ACTIVE *** ... forced by IDLETOKEN_FORCE_NO_NVML" diagnostic before returning NULL; a genuine missing driver retains the distinct "nvml.dll not found" diagnostic. Metal/Linux forced paths remain loud.

Lets a worker serve from mock weights instead of refusing. Refusal message names it; serving under it is labelled.
Serves a labelled mock completion when no engine is present. The reply itself carries the label, so it cannot be mistaken for inference.
Keeps a non-loopback API bind instead of rewriting it (hard constraint 5). Rewriting is the default and is announced; honouring it prints why.
Disables the Origin-header CSRF refusal for people genuinely building a browser front end. The 403 body names the variable, so the operator opts in knowingly.
Starts the engine after it reported the model does not fit. Prints a banner.

Lets an rpc-server start without a PSK. Prints loudly; without it the server refuses (hard constraint 10).
Turns on prompt logging, which is off by default. A privacy hatch, so the log itself is the loud evidence.
Selects the frozen ds4 backend instead of llama.cpp. Announced as loud in --help.
Pins each stage's layer range instead of using the planner. Prints "override active".
Stops the platform agent reporting cached prompt-prefix Bloom state. Announces itself on stderr and names PRIV-06; costs this machine prefix-affinity routing and cannot weaken a security verdict.

Names a directory with non-ASCII characters for the Windows UTF-8 path self-test (getenv, narrow CRT filesystem calls, AF_UNIX sun_path). Read ONLY inside windows_utf8_path_selftest(), which only --selftest reaches, and only on _WIN32; unset or empty returns immediately, so an ordinary --selftest stays portable. It selects a directory to probe, never a policy: no serving path reads it and it cannot relax a check.
